## Upstream changes 10.2.18 -> 10.2.19

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no upstream release notes were available for this version step, so breaking changes in the application cannot be ruled out from text; the image/registry diff itself shows only an expected version bump with no companion-service version named.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes — no notes were available to read (see below). This is not the same as "no breaking changes exist"; Atlassian's own release notes (published on their site, not GitHub) were not provided and have not been checked.

### Variables
- none found. The registry diff shows only `CONFLUENCE_VERSION` changing internally from '10.2.18' to '10.2.19', which matches the intended version bump and requires no action.
- Note for the host: the compose file's pin (`CONFLUENCE_IMAGE_VERSION:-10.2.18@sha256:f9230b44a82b779d7311a80ca49138df6edc160d44f4cf43035f9970875356be`) and the `.env.example` comment (`# CONFLUENCE_IMAGE_VERSION=10.2.18`) still reference 10.2.18 — moving to 10.2.19 requires updating the compose file's default pin (and digest) to 10.2.19, or setting `CONFLUENCE_IMAGE_VERSION`/`CONFLUENCE_IMAGE_TAG` in `.env` to override it.

### Data and dependencies
- none found in the notes. The compose file pins PostgreSQL 16 for the database; since no upstream notes were readable, there is no statement from Atlassian either confirming or contradicting compatibility with this Postgres version for 10.2.19. This is the one point to verify by hand before applying (see below) — if Atlassian's actual 10.2.19 release notes name a minimum or changed supported Postgres version, that would override this verdict.

### Before applying
- Manually check Atlassian's official Confluence 10.2.19 release notes and upgrade guide (they are not on GitHub) for: breaking changes, required manual steps, and the supported PostgreSQL version range.
- Take a database backup and a data-volume backup before upgrading (the stack's own `backups` service can be triggered manually, or confirm the scheduled backup is current).
- Update the compose file's `x-images` pin for `confluence` from `10.2.18@sha256:...` to the correct `10.2.19` tag and digest (or set `CONFLUENCE_IMAGE_VERSION=10.2.19` / `CONFLUENCE_IMAGE_TAG` in `.env`).
- After pulling, watch the Confluence container's startup logs and the `http://localhost:8090/` healthcheck for migration errors, since Confluence performs some upgrade tasks automatically on first boot of a new version.

### Notes read
- None. The release-notes source is listed as "not available: Atlassian publishes release notes on its own site, not on GitHub," and no UPGRADING, BREAKING_CHANGES or CHANGELOG section was supplied. What should be checked by hand instead: Atlassian's official Confluence Data Center/Server 10.2.19 release notes and the Confluence upgrade guide, specifically for supported database (PostgreSQL) version changes, deprecated features, and required pre-upgrade steps.

## Upstream changes v11.2.0 -> v11.3.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — new settings/update features touch environment behaviour this template manages by hand, and one bug fix changes the meaning of an env var the template does not set but operators may rely on.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes. The release is additive (new cloud/update/settings features) plus bug fixes; nothing in the notes announces a removed feature, changed default, or incompatible behaviour.

### Variables
- `DOZZLE_UPDATE_CONTAINERS` is named in the bug-fix list: "**settings**: DOZZLE_UPDATE_CONTAINERS, and read-only server settings that read as text". This variable is not referenced anywhere in the compose file or `.env.example`. The notes don't say whether it's new in this release or pre-existing and merely fixed; either way, nothing here needs editing unless the operator wants to opt into the new auto-update feature. Treat it as optional/unmanaged by this template.
- No other variable renames, removals, or new requirements are mentioned.

### Data and dependencies
- none. No companion-service version is named in the notes (no database, cache, or search engine), so the compose-pin mismatch rule does not apply here.
- The "WHAT THE IMAGES THEMSELVES DIFFER IN" section confirms `User`, `Entrypoint`, `Cmd`, `WorkingDir`, `ExposedPorts`, `Volumes`, `Healthcheck`, and environment are byte-for-byte identical between the two image builds. Whatever the release notes imply about new settings or update mechanisms, nothing about the container's invocation, exposed port (8080, matching the Traefik label), or the `/data` volume contract has changed. The existing `healthcheck: ["CMD", "/dozzle", "healthcheck"]` in the compose file remains valid as-is.

### Before applying
- No backup or migration step is required by the notes themselves.
- Because the new "Safe updates with rollback, auto-update modes, and reporting to Dozzle Cloud" feature (`https://github.com/amir20/dozzle/issues/5339`) and the cloud "fleet check" feature are new surface area that talks to Dozzle Cloud and can act on containers, confirm after upgrade that no auto-update mode is enabled by accident — this template's `dockerproxy` already denies `POST` by default (`POST: ${DOZZLE_DOCKERPROXY_POST:-0}`), which should keep any auto-update attempt from succeeding, but it's worth checking the new Settings pages after the upgrade to confirm nothing defaults to on.
- Update the pin: `DOZZLE_IMAGE_VERSION: v11.2.0@sha256:db7e19fd36189823c66239894e821561cb201248af35362ec6d39a08e23ff88b` → `v11.3.0@<new digest>` in the `x-images` block of the compose file, and fetch the real digest for v11.3.0 before deploying (the one in this review was not supplied).

### Notes read
- v11.3.0 (2026-10-05), compared against v11.2.0 via `https://github.com/amir20/dozzle/compare/v11.2.0...v11.3.0`. No UPGRADING, BREAKING_CHANGES, or CHANGELOG document was supplied separately from the release notes themselves — the release notes above are the only upgrade documentation available for this range.

## Upstream changes 1.37.3 -> 1.37.4

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — this release fixes multiple high/medium severity security advisories and carries several behavioural breaking changes that depend on this host's configuration; the image configuration itself is unchanged, so nothing at the container level needs adjusting, but the application-level changes need review before or right after applying.

### Breaking changes
- Reverse proxy IP determination changed: *"with `IP_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For`, the client IP is now the rightmost address that isn't in `IP_HEADER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (it used to be the leftmost)."* This compose stack puts Traefik directly in front of Vaultwarden with no `IP_HEADER`/`IP_HEADER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` set in `.env.example`, so if `IP_HEADER` is not set on this deployment this does not apply. If an operator has set `IP_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For` manually (not in the example file), rate limiting and logged IPs will change after upgrade unless `IP_HEADER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` is updated to list every proxy in the chain.
- `bw send receive` on CLI 2026.4.2 and older stops working: *"no longer works, the same as against Bitwarden's own servers since v2026.8.0."* Affects any users relying on the CLI for Sends, not an operator action, but worth flagging to users.
- Feature flags removed: *"`ssh-agent`, `ssh-key-vault-item`, `mutual-tls`, `anon-addy-self-host-alias`, `simple-login-self-host-alias`, `pm-25373-windows-biometrics-v2`, `pm-26340-linux-biometrics-v2`, `desktop-ui-migration-milestone-1` to `-4`, `cxp-import-mobile` and `cxp-export-mobile`"*. Not set via this compose/.env.example by default, but if `EXPERIMENTAL_CLIENT_FEATURE_FLAGS` was hand-set in `.env` to include any of these, *"startup logs a warning and saving settings in the admin panel fails until it's removed."*
- `DUO_USE_IFRAME` removed: *"the deprecated Traditional Prompt) is removed and ignored if set."* Not used in this compose file; only relevant if an operator added it manually.
- Two legacy API endpoints removed (`POST /identity/accounts/register`, `POST /api/accounts/prelogin`) — notes state no current client uses them.
- MariaDB/MySQL note: *"using the Alpine image of Vaultwarden might fail to connect [...] Add `MARIADB_TLS_DISABLE_PEER_VERIFICATION=1`"* — not applicable, this stack uses the SQLite backend (`db.sqlite3`, per the backups service).

### Variables
- No new required variables for this compose/.env.example setup. `IP_HEADER` / `IP_HEADER_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `EXPERIMENTAL_CLIENT_FEATURE_FLAGS`, `DUO_USE_IFRAME`, and `MARIADB_TLS_DISABLE_PEER_VERIFICATION` are not present in this repo's `.env.example` — only relevant if an operator has added them by hand outside the documented variables.

### Data and dependencies
- None. No database engine version is named in the release notes (this deployment uses SQLite via the bundled backup service, not an external database), no irreversible migration is mentioned, no port or path changes.

### Before applying
- Check whether `.env` sets `IP_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For` by hand; if so, update `IP_HEADER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` to include every proxy in front of Vaultwarden before/after upgrading.
- Check whether `.env` sets `EXPERIMENTAL_CLIENT_FEATURE_FLAGS`; if so, remove any of the now-dead flags listed above to avoid the admin panel save failure.
- After upgrading, if any organizations have admins who are not fully trusted, rotate the organization's API key per the note: *"consider rotating its API key after updating (Admin Console → Settings → Rotate API key). Before this release, Admins could also view the key."*
- Routine precaution: let the `backups` service complete one cycle (or trigger a manual snapshot) before restarting `vaultwarden`, since this is a security-fix release touching organization/cipher/attachment logic.

### Notes read
- Release notes for `1.37.4` (dani-garcia/vaultwarden), covering the 1.37.3 → 1.37.4 range. No separate UPGRADING/BREAKING_CHANGES file was supplied; the "Upgrade notes" section embedded in the 1.37.4 release notes was used as the authoritative breaking-change source.
